questions.prompt: You are writing a paragraph about the benefits of sport for teenagers. Which sentence is the best topic sentence to begin it?

options.text: Last Saturday I scored two goals in our school match.
Sport brings teenagers many important benefits.
My favourite player wears the number ten.
The school stadium is next to the main gate.

questions.explanation: A topic sentence announces the general idea of the whole paragraph, and "Sport brings teenagers many important benefits" covers everything the paragraph will prove. "Last Saturday I scored two goals in our school match" is about sport too, but it is one event — too narrow to cover the paragraph. A player and a stadium are details.

questions.prompt:
Put these sentences in the correct order to form a well-organised paragraph:

1. "Finally, fruit and vegetables keep the body strong."
2. "A healthy life depends on a few simple habits."
3. "First, sleeping eight hours helps the brain rest."

What is the best order?
questions.explanation: Sentence 2 is the most general, so it is the topic sentence and comes first. Then the order words guide you: "First" (3) comes before "Finally" (1). The best order is 2 – 3 – 1. Starting with "Finally" puts the end of the list at the beginning.

questions.prompt:
Choose the best linker to complete the sentence:

"The medicine tasted bitter, ___ the child swallowed it without a word."
questions.explanation: A bitter medicine makes us expect a refusal, yet the child swallows it: the two ideas are opposite, so a contrast linker is needed — "but". With "so" or "that's why", the bitter taste becomes the reason the child swallows the medicine, which is illogical; with "because", the swallowing becomes the cause of the taste.

questions.prompt:
Read this short paragraph about libraries:

"Public libraries are very useful. They lend books for free. They also offer a quiet place to study. My uncle prefers tea to coffee. Many pupils revise there before exams."

Which sentence is irrelevant and should be removed?

options.text: "They also offer a quiet place to study."

questions.explanation: The topic sentence says that libraries are useful, and every other sentence must prove it. Free books, a quiet place and revision before exams all do. "My uncle prefers tea to coffee" says nothing about libraries: it is irrelevant and breaks the unity of the paragraph.

questions.prompt:
Read the beginning of a paragraph:

"Smoking is dangerous for teenagers. It damages the lungs and makes young smokers tired quickly."

Which sentence is the most coherent continuation?

options.text: It also wastes their pocket money.
The weather in spring is usually pleasant.
My favourite colour has always been blue.
Cars need a lot of petrol to go from town to town.

questions.explanation: The paragraph lists the bad effects of smoking, so a coherent continuation adds another one: "It also wastes their pocket money" — "also" adds a new effect, and "it" still refers to smoking. The weather, a colour and cars change the topic and break the unity of the paragraph.

questions.prompt:
Choose the best linker to complete the passage:

"Many families sort their rubbish at home. ___ the streets of our town are cleaner."
questions.explanation: Clean streets follow from the sorting: the second sentence is the consequence, so it opens with a consequence linker — "So". "Because" introduces a cause, not a consequence. "Whereas" and "While" oppose two ideas, but sorting and clean streets are not opposite.
